subhead: Take a free practice quiz or point your phone at any TEAS 7 question for an instant, explained answer — reading, math, science, and English, without the guesswork.
metaDescription: Free TEAS 7 quiz and practice questions with instant, explained answers. Reading, mathematics, science, and English & language usage sections.
whyItWorks: TEAS 7 tests whether you can quickly and accurately apply reading comprehension, basic math, and science reasoning under time pressure — exactly the speed-plus-accuracy skill nursing programs use the exam to predict. Cambo reads the exact question and shows the reasoning, so you can see exactly where a wrong answer went wrong instead of just memorizing the right one.

sampleQuestions.q: A prescription label reads: "Take 2 tablets by mouth every 6 hours as needed for pain, not to exceed 8 tablets in 24 hours." Based on this label, what is the MAXIMUM number of doses a patient may take in one day?
sampleQuestions.a: 4 doses — 8 tablets maximum divided by 2 tablets per dose equals 4 doses in 24 hours.

sampleQuestions.q: A patient's weight is 154 pounds. What is this weight in kilograms (1 kg ≈ 2.2 lb)?
Which blood component is primarily responsible for carrying oxygen to body tissues?
sampleQuestions.a: Red blood cells — they contain hemoglobin, the protein that binds oxygen in the lungs and releases it to tissues throughout the body.

sampleQuestions.q: Which of the following is the correct order of the digestive process, from first to last?
options: Stomach, mouth, small intestine, large intestine
Mouth, stomach, small intestine, large intestine
Mouth, small intestine, stomach, large intestine
Large intestine, stomach, small intestine, mouth
sampleQuestions.a: Mouth, stomach, small intestine, large intestine — food is chewed and enters the stomach for initial digestion, then nutrients are absorbed in the small intestine before waste moves through the large intestine.

options: The patient's chart which was updated this morning showed improved vital signs.
The patient's chart, which was updated this morning, showed improved vital signs.
The patient's chart, which was updated this morning showed improved vital signs.
The patient's chart which was updated this morning, showed improved vital signs.
sampleQuestions.a: The second option — the nonessential clause "which was updated this morning" needs a comma both before and after it to be set off correctly.

faqs.q: How many questions are on the TEAS 7?
faqs.a: 170 questions across four sections (Reading, Mathematics, Science, and English & Language Usage) in 209 minutes; about 150 are scored and 20 are unscored pilot questions.

faqs.q: What score do I need to pass the TEAS 7?
faqs.a: There's no universal passing score set by ATI — each nursing or allied health program sets its own minimum composite score, commonly in the 60-75% range.

faqs.q: What sections are on the TEAS 7?
faqs.a: Reading (45 questions), Mathematics (38 questions), Science (50 questions), and English & Language Usage (37 questions).

faqs.q: Is Cambo affiliated with ATI Testing?
faqs.a: No. Cambo is an independent study tool and isn't produced, endorsed, or affiliated with Assessment Technologies Institute (ATI), publisher of the TEAS exam.

faqs.q: How many times can I retake the TEAS 7?
faqs.a: ATI itself doesn't cap attempts, but individual nursing programs set their own retake limits and waiting periods — commonly two to three attempts per year, with at least 14 days between attempts.

faqs.q: Do I need to take the TEAS before nursing school?
faqs.a: Most nursing and allied health programs require a TEAS score as part of admission, since it's designed to predict readiness for program coursework — check your specific program's requirement and minimum score.
